question: Does the reported benefit generalize beyond disease-specific KGs (Gastroparesis, Diabetes) to standard multi-hop KGQA benchmarks, and is the 3-5-hop evaluation set large and independent enough to support the claim?
description: The retrieved closest work validates only on two disease-specific KGs built by GraphMERT, and reports reaching 100% accuracy on cleaned retained one-hop validation sets. Retained sets are cleaned using information from the repair loop, so near-perfect one-hop accuracy may reflect selection on the evaluation set rather than genuine factual grounding, and the deeper-hop sets may be small. Whether the effect holds on standard benchmarks (e.g., WebQSP, ComplexWebQuestions, MetaQA) and under a held-out, non-retained split is the main external-validity question.
rationale: External validity determines whether the contribution is a general mechanism or a domain artifact; standard-benchmark evidence has not yet been retrieved, and the 'retained' validation-set construction is a plausible evaluation confounder.
